messages.subject: Bayesian sparse mixed-model
parts:
Hi,
Is it possible with INLA to fit a model like y = X%*%beta + Z%*%b+e with beta is parametrized as a mixture of two Gaussian: one with a sharp peak at 0 and one with a larger variance. The idea is to model most coefficients as very small and a few with larger effects.

Thanks in advance.

Regards,
Inti

thanks for that quick response.

Another model I would like to try is 
 y = X%*%beta + Z%*%b+ e_{1}

 beta =T%*%gamma + e_{2}

with X and T a matrices with predictors.

I am thinking I would set a gaussian prior on beta with a small std-deviation and let the second level regression on the betas to help push some coefficients to larger values.

Can this be fitted with INLA? how would the formula look like?

In my case size of beta will be in order of 10^5 - 10^6, size of gamma in the order of 10^4 and size of y of 10^3-10^4. Do you think it would be possible to fit this regression on R-INLA?

Thanks a lot in advance,
Inti

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Bayesian sparse mixed-model
parts:
On Wed, 2013-08-07 at 13:11 +0100, Inti Pedroso wrote:
> thanks for that quick response.
>
> Another model I would like to try is
> y = X%*%beta + Z%*%b+ e_{1}
>
> beta =T%*%gamma + e_{2}
>
> with X and T a matrices with predictors.

if you write the second one as

0 = T %*% gamma + e_2

then the mean is T%*% gamma observed with 0's and prec(e_2).

so you can write this jointly as (making ';' means 'newline')


[y] = [ X, Z] %*% [beta] + [e_1]
[0] [ T, 0] [b ] [e_2]


with hopefully understandable notation

so you get two likelihoods, and use the A matrix to implement the model
